objective: Test whether the hard-pair criterion of CLASSK-DICHOTOMY-20261026-001 extends past class 2, for G = N x| C_r with N of class 3 and exponent p (p >= 5, r | p - 1, coprime split action). Two discriminators: (1) a class-3 group whose class-2 quotient has no hard pair but whose bracket between layers one and two joins nontrivial characters with nontrivial product (expected #P-hard by reduction to the Heisenberg count, so the criterion must live in the associated graded); (2) a group with no hard pair in any layer whose layer-3 obstruction is a twisted triple Massey product, a four-way interaction among characters alpha, alpha^-1, alpha^-1, alpha (hard means the boundary is 'three or more', easy means graded hard pairs suffice). Approved by the owner on 2026-10-27 ('Yes, let's continue') after the class-(K) dichotomy.
status: Complete: both discriminators past class 2 are hard. A cross-layer hard pair in the associated graded makes counting #P-hard (A). A four-way twisted Massey interaction does too where no pair can be hard: U4(F_p) x| <diag(1,-1,1,-1)> on 2-surgeries of knots, p >= 5 (C, realization supported by B). So the line past class 2 is not three-way pairs. Next (r = 2 dichotomy in every class, 2/3) awaits the owner.
stop_rule: Stop when both discriminators are decided (each by a proof of #P-hardness, a proof of a polynomial algorithm, or a substantive obstruction to the route), and report the resulting criterion and its precise gaps.
title: Counting maps to coprime p-group-by-cyclic groups past class 2: cross-layer pairs and four-way Massey interactions
